title: Asynchronous Skill-Spotlight Interview Circuit & Credential Badging
body:
Purpose: quick experiment doc for an asynchronous interview circuit focused on narrow technical skills + a lightweight micro-credential (badge) that can speed hiring and reduce live panel load. Draft for feedback from hiring managers + solutions eng.

Context / why this: we keep seeing ramp friction for cross-pool hires (infra -> serving-runtime, se -> product). Live panels are expensive and blockers for candidates on different timezones. Goal: capture objective signals for 3–4 core skills via asynchronous tasks + a short live calibration interview only when needed. If candidate clears the circuit, they earn a temporary micro-credential that reduces downstream interview stages (fewer loops, faster offer decision).

Scope: IC-level roles (IC2–IC4), early experiments for SRE, Platform Eng, and Solutions Eng hires. Not intended for senior staff/manager roles in this phase.

High-level flow (candidate perspective):
- Apply -> short recruiter screen (30m) to confirm role fit and logistics.
- Candidate receives Skill Circuit link with 3 cards (each 30–45m):
  1) Architecture sketch (whiteboard-style doc + 1 annotated design) — evaluate tradeoffs and constraints.
  2) Hands-on snippet (code/config) — small terraform/helm or python inference stub to fix/complete.
  3) Observation & incident triage (logs + timeline) — ask for root-cause and containment steps.
- Candidate uploads answers within 72 hours (accept longer for timezone / schedule needs).
- Asynchronous reviewers (People Ops pool + 1 hiring-manager reviewer) score against rubric.
- If pass threshold => award "Redwood Skill-Spotlight (role: infra/ops)" micro-credential valid for 6 months.
- Micro-credential reduces onsite panel from 5->3 interviews and short-circuits the initial technical deep-dive.

Why asynchronous pieces chosen:
- Architecture sketch captures system design judgment without long live sessions.
- Code/config snippet tests practical familiarity with our infra patterns and quick debugging.
- Incident triage stresses telemetry interpretation and prioritization — signals on production readiness.

Rubric (scoring is 0/1/2 per sub-item; final threshold >= 14/18 to pass):
- Architecture sketch (6 points total):
  - Problem scoping: 0/1/2 (clarity, assumptions)
  - Tradeoff articulation: 0/1/2 (latency/cost/reliability balance)
  - Compatibility with Redwood infra: 0/1/2 (security, deploy patterns)
- Code/config snippet (6 points):
  - Correctness: 0/1/2
  - Simplicity/readability: 0/1/2
  - Edge cases/tests: 0/1/2
- Incident triage (6 points):
  - Root cause reasoning: 0/1/2
  - Containment/action plan: 0/1/2
  - Communication & stakeholder prioritization: 0/1/2

Reviewer guidance (short):
- Use first-pass 10-minute read per submission; mark obvious red flags (plagiarism / pasted solutions) and escalate.
- Look for pragmatic tradeoffs — we prefer safe deterministic solutions over clever but brittle hacks.
- If reviewer score range between reviewers > 3 points, trigger a 20-minute calibration sync with hiring manager.

Micro-credential mechanics:
- Badge metadata: role tag, issuance date, expiry date (6 months), issuing reviewer(s) list.
- Stored in internal People Ops badge registry (CSV / Okta attribute prototype).
- Badge reduces interview loop: removes initial deep algorithmic/system-design panel and reserves 1 behavioral + 1 system validation interview.
- Badge is not an automatic hire decision — hiring manager still reviews other signals (culture fit, salary alignment).

Onboarding checklist for candidates who arrive with the badge (first 14 days condensed):
- Day 0: preboarding packet + service accounts created (people-ops label: skill-spotlight).
- Day 1: 60m role orientation + access walkthrough with platform buddy.
- Day 2–3: focused infra priming lab (2h self-paced exercises) — validate retained skills from the circuit.
- Day 4–7: paired shadowing with oncall buddy (observe incident runbook and deploy process).
- End of week 2: light evaluation check-in with hiring manager (30m) — confirm badge signals matched real tasks.

Operational notes / TODOs (open items):
- Decide hosting: Google Form + private GDrive for uploads vs short-lived Codesandbox/Cloud Shell links.
- Anti-cheat: require candidate to sign an attest statement; random sampling for live code verification if suspicious.
- Badge storage: prototype in HRIS (Workday/Greenhouse) vs People Ops internal sheet. Need legal on PII retention.
- Owner: People Ops to run first 60 candidates; propose monthly calibration sessions with hiring managers.

Pilot metrics (how we'll measure success):
- Time-to-offer delta for badge vs non-badge candidates (target: -25% median time).
- Panel interviewer-hours saved per candidate (target: save 2–3 hours per hire).
- Badge precision: percent of badge-holders who pass first 3 months performance check (target: >=80%).
- Candidate satisfaction (NPS-like question post-interview) — aim >= 7/10.

Sample asynchronous prompts (short):
- Arch prompt: "Design a request-routing layer for model inference that handles multi-tenant caching, per-tenant rate limits, and has a graceful degradation path when GPU pool saturated. Annotate where you'd add metrics and circuit-breakers."
- Code prompt: "Given this minimal LLM-serving pseudocode, fix the memory leak and add a unit test for the token cache eviction policy."
- Triage prompt: "You see a 30% latency tail increase for embeddings in EU region after a deploy. Logs show sporadic KV timeout errors. Write a 5-step immediate mitigation and a 3-week remediation plan."

Calibration and fairness considerations:
- Ensure tasks are role-relevant and language-neutral where possible (avoid long prose-heavy answers for non-communications roles).
- We will recruit a diverse reviewer pool and require blinded grading (remove name/LinkedIn from submissions during rubric scoring).
- Translation/adjusted timelines for candidates in APAC / EMEA — allow extra submission time if requested.

Notes to self / meeting sparks:
- Run 2-week trial with 30 candidates across SRE + Solutions Eng; iterate prompts based on common confusions.
- Coordinate with Growth to advertise fast-track for community contributors (open-source maintainers) as pilot cohort.
- Draft email templates for recruiters and candidate-facing instructions.

Appendix (links):
- Prototype prompt bank: https://docs.google.com/document/d/skill-spotlight-proto
- Reviewer score sheet template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/score-sheet
- Initial legal note: internal/people-ops/legal-privacy-slim

Status: rough working draft — looking for feedback on rubric thresholds, badge expiry policy, and storage approach.

-- Maya (people-ops)
